Blocking Coalitions

Drag the division around and watch who objects. If some group can object, the division falls. If one 🧑 person ends up worse than going alone, that person walks out. If a group can split things better together, it falls too. Only divisions nobody can walk away from survive. That surviving set is the core. For example, three friends split 10 🍬 candies. If one friend gets only 1 candy, that friend walks away. If two friends secretly find a better split, the original split collapses. Only a split nobody wants to leave stays standing.

x∈core  ⟺  no S blocks xx \in \text{core} \iff \text{no } S \text{ blocks } xx∈core⟺no S blocks x

Examples & Exercises

With the allocation x1=(7,3)x^1 = (7, 3)x1=(7,3) (i.e., the endowment itself), determine which coalition blocks it.

MRS1(7,3)=3/7≠7/3=MRS2(3,7)MRS_1(7,3) = 3/7 \ne 7/3 = MRS_2(3,7)MRS1​(7,3)=3/7=7/3=MRS2​(3,7)
Show proof
  1. u1=u2=21≈4.58u_1 = u_2 = \sqrt{21} \approx 4.58u1​=u2​=21​≈4.58: individual rationality holds, so neither {1}\{1\}{1} nor {2}\{2\}{2} blocks.
  2. But MRS1=3/7≠7/3=MRS2MRS_1 = 3/7 \ne 7/3 = MRS_2MRS1​=3/7=7/3=MRS2​: Pareto inefficient. Moving to x1=(5,5)x^1 = (5, 5)x1=(5,5) gives u1=u2=5>4.58u_1 = u_2 = 5 > 4.58u1​=u2​=5>4.58, so the grand coalition {1,2}\{1, 2\}{1,2} blocks — the lens in the picture is exactly that Pareto-improving set.

Verify that no coalition can block the allocation x1=(5,5)x^1 = (5, 5)x1=(5,5).

Show proof
  1. u1=u2=5>4.58=ui(ei)u_1 = u_2 = 5 > 4.58 = u_i(e^i)u1​=u2​=5>4.58=ui​(ei): individually rational, so {1}\{1\}{1}, {2}\{2\}{2} cannot block.
  2. MRS1(5,5)=MRS2(5,5)=1MRS_1(5,5) = MRS_2(5,5) = 1MRS1​(5,5)=MRS2​(5,5)=1: on the contract curve and Pareto efficient, so {1,2}\{1, 2\}{1,2} cannot block either. Hence (5,5)(5, 5)(5,5) is in the core (indeed, it is the competitive equilibrium).
